name: REGISTRAR'S ARCHIVE
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE STACKS
LOOK_AT: Shelves to the ceiling, every claim and quarrel in the district folded into brown paper. The town's entire memory, filed under mostly the wrong letters.
Every claim ever filed in this district, in boxes, in order. It is the most organized thing in Consolation and no one is permitted to look at it.
The boxes for the first year are the thinnest. It took the town a year to start lying in quantity.
LISTEN_TO: Settling. An archive breathes about once an hour.
Nothing. Paper does not keep secrets so much as decline to volunteer.
A box settling on a high shelf. The archive, turning over in its sleep.

overrides.PULL: One folder is never one folder. The stacks are an ecosystem and I am not licensed to hunt in it.

subjects.name: THE FILING LADDER
LOOK_AT: A ladder on a rail, for reaching the years nobody asks about. The wheels are rusted at 1858 and shine at the present.
The rungs are worn smooth in the middle, the way rungs are.
From the top rung you can touch the ceiling and the oldest box in the district at once.
LISTEN_TO: The rail, ticking as the building cools.
A wheel squeaking a quarter turn as I lean on it.
Nothing. It has been put back exactly where it was, which is to say, used.

overrides.PUSH: It rolls to 1858 and stops of its own accord, like a horse that knows the route.

subjects.name: THE MOTT FILE
LOOK_AT: The famous filing. The original declaration of the strike, under glass now, because people kept touching it. The signature is confident. The rest is brief.

One sheet. A date, a name, an assertion, and a signature. There is no location on it. There has never been a location on it. Ten thousand men have dug for twelve years on the strength of a sheet of paper that does not say where.
It is shorter than my letter to my mother. It has done considerably more.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. It has said what it has to say for twelve years.
Nothing at all.
Nothing. Twelve years under glass, and still nothing to add.

overrides.OPEN: Under glass, and the glass is under Sump, and Sump is under statute. It is the best-defended document in the territory.

subjects.name: THE TIMESHEET
LOOK_AT: The watch rota for the year of the strike, kept for no reason anyone remembers. Names, nights, initials.
The watchman's hours, signed weekly. Twelve years of them, in a stack.
Bundled with string and labeled by year. The archive keeps everything, including what nobody asked it to keep.
LISTEN_TO: Paper. Same hand as the filing.
Paper. Same hand as the filing.
Paper. Same hand as the filing.

subjects.name: THE COUNTY SEAL
LOOK_AT: The seal that makes paper true. A pound of brass with the weight of scripture. Sump cleans it more often than it needs.
The handle is wrapped in chamois so it will not mark. Even the seal is handled with care.
Around the rim, CONSOLATION COUNTY; in the middle, a pickaxe crossed with a quill. That is the whole economy, and it is accurate.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. It speaks only when pressed.
Nothing. It is resting between truths.
A faint ring when I set it down. Brass, agreeing with itself.

overrides.USE: I lifted it an inch. The weight of it is a legal argument. I set it down persuaded.

subjects.name: THE UNCLAIMED CORRESPONDENCE
LOOK_AT: A pigeonhole of letters addressed to men the territory has misplaced. Some have waited years. The postage is a small museum.
One is addressed to Ezra Pike. Six years waiting. I carried its twin eleven hundred miles.
Some envelopes have been readdressed three times, each to a camp further west. The last is addressed to nowhere at all, and was delivered here.
LISTEN_TO: Envelopes. Patience, in paper form.
A soft slither as one envelope leans into another.
Nothing. Letters keep very quiet when nobody is coming for them.

overrides.PICK_UP: Other men's letters. I have one of my own addressed to a dead man; I know how they feel about being held.

subjects.name: THE DAMP CORNER
LOOK_AT: The roof lets go here in the wet months, and the records of 1851 have paid for it. The town's third year is a soft gray brick.
A bucket under the worst of it, half full, and a second bucket under the first bucket's overflow.
Whatever was filed in 1851 is legible only as a color now: a soft brown peace.
LISTEN_TO: A drip, in season. Today it is only thinking about it.
A single drop, at last, into the bucket. It had been thinking about it for some time.
Nothing. The roof is saving up.

subjects.name: THE CLERK'S DESK
LOOK_AT: Sump's desk in the archive, angled so he can see the door and the door cannot see what he is reading.
A blotter, a pen and a stamp pad, all squared to the edge. Sump's archive desk is Sump in furniture.
One drawer has a brass label: PENDING. It is empty. Nothing in Sump's charge is pending for long.
LISTEN_TO: A drawer that does not quite shut. It holds something read often.
The drawer that will not quite shut, ticking when the floor moves.
Nothing. Sump's desk is quiet even when he is not at it.

subjects.name: THE LAMP BRACKET
LOOK_AT: No open flame in the archive; the lamp lives in a bracket by the door, and the deep stacks stay dark. What the archive knows, it knows in the dark.
The wall above it is scorched in a neat oval, the shape of a lamp held at that height for a long time.
It is the only light allowed in here, and it is allowed only as far as the door.
LISTEN_TO: The bracket rocks a little. Someone takes the lamp down more than Sump admits.
The bracket creaking as the door swings.
Nothing. The lamp is down, and the bracket is waiting for it.

subjects.name: CLAIM ONE'S BOX
LOOK_AT: The most famous claim in the territory. The box is the same size as all the others, which I find unreasonable.
It has a brass corner piece, which none of the others has. Somebody felt the most famous box deserved a little armor.
The label is in Sump's hand, and has been relabeled once, in Sump's hand, more neatly.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing.
Nothing. A box holding one sheet makes the same sound as an empty one.
Nothing. The most famous box in the territory has nothing to say for itself.

subjects.name: THE EXECUTORS' LEDGER
LOOK_AT: A record of every man who has entered this room. Nineteen names. I am the twentieth, and I am dead.
The ink of the last entry before mine is years old. Nobody has been dead enough to come in here for a long time.
I signed it. Under occupation I wrote 'deceased', because it seemed the honest thing.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing.
Nothing. A book of visitors, none of whom is visiting.
The page settling as I close it. Twenty names now, and one of them still breathing.

subjects.name: THE BARRED WINDOW
LOOK_AT: Barred, on the inside. Whoever built this was not worried about people getting in.
The bars are set in mortar on the inside of the frame. Somebody built a room to keep paper from escaping.
Through the bars, a slice of Main Street: one hitching rail, one horse, one man looking at neither.
LISTEN_TO: Main Street. Muffled. It sounds like a town from in here.
A wagon passing, reduced to a rumor.
Somebody laughing outside. In here it sounds like a story about someone else.

subjects.name: THE DUST
LOOK_AT: Undisturbed everywhere except one shelf, at chest height, where somebody has been reaching for years.
It lies on everything else like a sheet over the furniture in a closed house.
My own prints are in it now. It will remember me longer than the town does.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing.
Nothing. Dust is very good at being undisturbed.
Nothing. I sneezed once, which is the loudest thing this room has heard in a year.

subjects.name: THE CHAIR
LOOK_AT: One chair. Facing the shelves. Somebody sits in here.
A plain chair with a cushion worn flat in the shape of one particular person.
I did not sit in it. It felt like someone else's.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. It has been sat in a great deal and it is not saying by whom.
A creak as the cushion lets go of the last shape it held.
Nothing. It is waiting for whoever it waits for.
